subject: frostAxe
pitch:
Category: Fantasy weapon.
Subject: frost-forged battle axe.
Style: League of Legends.
reasoning:
I'm checking the render for issues — the blade extrude looks okay despite a somewhat jagged fluke, but the fur ring is coming out grey instead of white, likely due to how the shading interacts with the outward-facing normals on the cards.

I'm considering adding a slight emissive glow (around 0.35 intensity) to brighten the fur without flattening it. The banners hanging off the fur look fine overlapping the grip wrap, but the haft's dark purple is barely readable, so I want to shift it to a brighter icy wood tone like "#6a5a8c" or "#3a2e58". The leather wrap spiral and gold band placement check out fine, and I'm now looking at whether the blade's cyan hexagon inlay reads as too flat.

The inlay could use a gradient rather than a solid bright glow, so I'm dialing the emissive down slightly. The spear point, socket pieces, axe head scale, and plinth rocks all look proportionate and fine as-is. For the blade itself, I'm thinking about adding a thin glowing frost-rim extrude along the cutting edge to give it more definition instead of a flat gradient fade.

Writing outline coordinates...

I'll add a slight bevel to soften the blade edge and keep the glow stylized rather than overly thick. The rest—fur brightness, haft color, plinth decals, socket runes—all look fine as is, so I'll skip adding an extra glowing orb or icy pool to avoid overcomplicating the design.

Now I'm wrapping the cards loop with a glow effect, targeting the fur material since its light color will read well with a soft 0.45 glow. I need to find the exact closing lines of that loop to insert the glow call correctly, then place the rim glow block right before the glowing inlay section.
